title: PR decomposition lab notes — inference refactor risk lens
content:
Notes to self: high-level goal = split the big inference-config change into minimally risky pieces and outline tests/observability so rollback is surgical. Use a "decomposition lens": map each change to risk vectors and simple mitigation.

Overview of PR: refactor batching + kv-cache handling to allow adaptive batch sizing per-model and introduce a per-model config object that flows from config service -> runtime. Big wins: better P99 for short-requests, potential cost down via better batching. Big risk: subtle cache invalidation bugs, token-order/kv mismatch, increased GC pressure.

Risk vectors (quick scores 1 low - 5 high):
- Correctness (kv/cache semantics): 5
- Latency regressions: 3
- Memory/GC pressure: 4
- Backward compatibility (old config): 2
- Observability/diagnosability: 2
- Rollback complexity: 3

Decomposition plan (atomic pieces + why):
1) Introduce config object skeleton (no behavior change).
   - Move constants into typed struct, wire via DI but default to old behavior.
   - Tests: unit tests for defaulting logic, linting.
   - Rollback: trivial (revert wiring).
2) Add adaptive batch-size decision hook (pure function).
   - Implement as library function, keep runtime callsites unchanged.
   - Tests: unit for heuristic (simulate distributions), small integration test under stress harness.
   - Risk: if heuristic chosen wrong, latency could increase — keep behind feature flag.
3) KV-cache integration switch (opt-in).
   - New API field: cache_version_hint, not used until opt-in.
   - Tests: validation that old clients still accept requests.
   - Rollout: canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% with automatic rollback on error rate.
4) Memory accounting + guardrails (conservative caps).
   - Add counters + eviction thresholds.
   - Tests: synthetic load to assert caps respected.

Checklist before merging each piece:
- [ ] Unit tests + smoke tests added
- [ ] Benchmarks: baseline and after change (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec) captured and uploaded to PR
- [ ] Memory profile snapshot under load (heap/alloc rate)
- [ ] Add metrics hooks: cache_hits, cache_misses, cache_evictions, batch_size_histogram
- [ ] Tracing: annotate span for batch decision + cache path
- [ ] Add feature flag + config toggle with default off for big change
- [ ] Updated docs for runtime config and migration notes

Suggested quick experiments to validate heuristics (local cluster):
- Synthetic mix: 70% short requests (<=32 tokens), 20% med (32-256), 10% long (>256). Run 5m sweeps with different heuristic weights.
- Commands:
  - bench harness: ./tools/bench --profile=short-heavy --parallel=32 --duration=300
  - memory run: docker-compose up --scale runtime=4; ./scripts/mem-smoke.sh --threads 64

Observability snippets (queries to add to dashboard):
- cache_hit_rate = sum(cache_hits) / (sum(cache_hits) + sum(cache_misses))
- avg_batch_size = histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- rollback_trigger = increase(error_count[5m]) > 5% baseline

Rollback criteria (explicit):
- Error rate > 0.5% absolute increase for > 3 consecutive 1m windows OR
- p99 latency regression > 25% for > 5m OR
- Memory usage > baseline + 30% sustained for 2m

Post-merge follow-ups (short list):
- If cache evictions spike: add TTL & per-model eviction prioritization
- If small requests latency still high: consider micro-batching fallback under 10ms boundary
- If GC spikes: move blob allocations to arena pool (proof-of-concept branch exists: gc-arena-wip)

Open questions / TODOs (need quick sync w/ Diego):
- Compatibility with dedicated deployment routing (Dedicated uses different config path) — ensure config service change is backward compatible.
- Should we bump protocol version when cache_version_hint is present? pros/cons? (Diego thinks no, because we use feature flags)
- Appetite for automated canary rollback vs manual (ops capacity) — ping SRE.

Small code examples to show safe wiring (pseudocode):
- old callsite: serve(req) { let decision = pick_batch_size(req); call_infer(req, decision); }
- new (phase 1): serve(req) { let cfg = Config.fromContext(req.ctx).withDefaults(); let decision = batch_heuristic(cfg, req); call_infer(req, decision); }

Pre-merge PR checklist for reviewers (short):
- Do changes preserve current config defaults? Try live request against dev cluster.
- Is the cache key invariant preserved (sequence id + model + session)?
- Are metrics + traces sufficient to triage if rollback needed?
- Are locks/atomic updates around cache insertions safe across threads?

Notes-to-self on review style: be explicit about "accept iff" conditions in comments. For every change that touches cache/ordering, demand an integration test that reproduces the bug we fear (e.g., interleaved writes causing stale kv reads).

If this goes poorly: emergency plan: revert config wiring, enable conservative global caps, and shift traffic to dedicated fallback pool (Dedicated has slightly higher latency but stable behavior). Prepare a backfill ticket to ensure analytics capture exact affected requests.

Links I should paste into PR description later:
- perf baseline: https://perf.redwood/bench/2024-10-10/baseline
- mem snapshot: gcs://redwood-mem-dumps/2024-10-11/heap.prof
- related RFC: confluence.redwood/inference-cache-rfc

Random scratchpad notes:
- consider 'safe-mode' where batch size can't exceed X for first N seconds after deployment
- avoid rolling changes to both batching and cache in same minute (hard to debug)

End of notes. Next action: split PR into 3 PRs as above. Schedule 30m sync with Diego + SRE this week.
